set.n: Civil War soldier's coins under the old granary, D. K. Smalling farm (found 1904)
set.st: August 1904: nearly $300 in coin was gathered where it "oozed out of the soil" at the old granary site on the D. K. Smalling farm. It was believed hidden about 30 years earlier by J. H. Parsons, who buried it when he went to war and never recovered it. Smalling dug out 'a large quantity' (the cloth sack had rotted). Recovered Aug 1904; nothing reported left. Pin is approximate, not the spot itself.
set.t: FOUND 1904. Smalling had two 80s in sec 5 on the 1910 atlas; the old granary site is on one of them. Access: private.

src: Waterloo Courier, 13 Aug 1904, p. 1 'Coin Found in Ground' (Newspapers.com 356436400)

set.tovw: One wire, no find; robbery Jan 1916; farm placed from the 1913 Jo Daviess atlas
set.t: Earlier wire copies said 'near Dubuque', but the Dubuque special and the Freeport paper put him in Illinois, north of Galena. The copies are one wire family, so C on the placed farm. The Illinois Central line runs through East Galena, which fits the placement. Dubuque papers 1880-1927 are not indexed. The money was said to be hidden about the cabin, not on him. Find the cabin on a 1910s Jo Daviess plat (the 1925 plat may show the land under a later owner) or in the Galena Gazette for Jan 1916. Private land: ask permission.

set.pl: 1836 E Lincoln Hwy, east edge of DeKalb (1940 census address; same residence 1935)
set.t: Private house/farm lot; one building near the road with a long drive behind (aerial, PC read); outcome unknown. Access: private: permission.
set.st: Ray Yocum, 42, a garage owner, buried a fruit jar with $2,300 in $100 bills in the yard of his East Lincoln Highway home in DeKalb one night in Nov 1938 and could not find it again. He denied the rumour for two months and was still digging in mid-July 1939; no recovery found in papers 1939-50. The 1940 census has Ray and Lillian Yocum owning a small farm ($2,500) at 1836 East Lincoln Highway, the same place as in 1935, so the jar went into that yard at the east edge of town.

set.pl: South First Street, Marshalltown (hut site; block unknown)
set.tovw: One wire; hut burned 1907; brother denied wealth
set.st: Honora McKnight, about 90, burned to death in her hut on South First Street, Marshalltown, in May 1907. A hospital sister had seen her take an apron full of $20 gold pieces from under the faggots in her kitchen wood box; her brother Martin Griffin of Savanna ridiculed the wealth story. The money, if any, was in the hut that burned. Pin is on the street, not the hut.

src: Marshalltown Evening Times-Republican, 6 May 1907, p. 7 'Kept Money in Wood Box' (Newspapers.com 352734265; wire copy Davenport Daily Times 8 May p. 2, 299667563)
